Given:
- Speed of particles, $v = 2.8 \times 10^8 \text{ m/s}$
- Relativistic lifetime (measured in lab), $t = 2.5 \times 10^{-7} \text{ s}$
- Speed of light, $c = 3 \times 10^8 \text{ m/s}$

Using the time dilation formula:
$$t = \frac{t_0}{\sqrt{1 - \frac{v^2}{c^2}}}$$

Where $t_0$ is the proper lifetime. Rearranging for $t_0$:
$$t_0 = t \sqrt{1 - \frac{v^2}{c^2}}$$

First, calculate $\frac{v}{c}$:
$$\frac{v}{c} = \frac{2.8 \times 10^8}{3 \times 10^8} = \frac{28}{30} = 0.9333$$

Substitute values:
$$t_0 = (2.5 \times 10^{-7}) \sqrt{1 - (0.9333)^2} = (2.5 \times 10^{-7}) \sqrt{1 - 0.8711}$$
$$t_0 = (2.5 \times 10^{-7}) \sqrt{0.1289} = (2.5 \times 10^{-7}) (0.359) \approx 8.97 \times 10^{-8} \text{ s}$$

**Proper lifetime ($t_0$)** $\approx 8.97 \times 10^{-8} \text{ s}$.
proTip: Always remember that proper time ($t_0$) is measured in the frame where the clock is at rest, hence it is always smaller than the dilated time ($t$).
